approval.cost: No fee for building/publishing an integration is stated in the docs; the Marketplace (a commercial platform where partners sell offerings) has 'additional fees' billed to customers; partner-side program fees are not stated
approval.trigger: Two gates. (a) Partner gate: you must join the Datadog Partner Network (Technology Partner track; per the Marketplace docs you apply and must be approved before building a Marketplace offering) and get a partner developer organization/sandbox ('Creating a developer sandbox may take up to one or two business days'). (b) Listing review: 'Submit your integration for review. After approval, Datadog publishes it', and 'The Datadog team will review and respond with feedback'. Pre-publication cap (functional, not numeric): 'Until an OAuth client is published, you can only authorize the client from the partner developer organization it was created in' (attempting otherwise yields invalid_request, Invalid client_id).
approval.wait: Not stated in the docs (sandbox provisioning 'up to one or two business days' is the only stated duration; a separate partner-program website outside the docs quotes 4-6 weeks to publish, flagged as unverified here)

blockers.detail: 'OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.' No partner status means no OAuth, period; everyone else uses API keys + application keys per organization.
blockers.howToClear: Apply to the Datadog Partner Network (Technology Partner track) and get a partner developer organization before designing anything around OAuth.
blockers.title: The partner gate is absolute

blockers.detail: 'Your product must direct users to initiate the OAuth flow from Datadog, so Datadog can provide the domain and site parameters to your onboarding URL. These parameters are not included if the flow starts from your product.' A 'Connect Datadog' button hosted purely in your own product breaks the documented model. Also: 'Datadog does not support multi-tenanted applications where customers authorize using individual subdomains; authorization is supported only through a single domain.'
blockers.howToClear: Design onboarding around the Datadog tile as the entry point, and a single authorization domain.
blockers.title: The flow must start inside Datadog

blockers.detail: OAuth tokens alone cannot ingest data: during the handshake you request the api_keys_write scope and call POST /api/v2/api_keys/marketplace to create an API key on behalf of the user ('the only way to send data into Datadog through OAuth'). Only one such key can exist per organization, its value is shown once, and if lost you must revoke it and have the user reinstall/re-authorize. api_keys_write is described as a private scope; if you can't set it, Datadog tells you to email marketplace@datadoghq.com.
blockers.howToClear: Build the key-minting step into the handshake and vault the key at creation.
blockers.title: Data submission detours through API keys

Some pages were read in full; the OAuth2 endpoints reference, OAuth2-in-Datadog, scopes, integrations overview, and Marketplace pages were read via official docs excerpts, as noted in the research report.
unverified: Review/publish timeline: no duration stated in the docs pages read. (Datadog's separate partner-program website, outside docs.datadoghq.com, quotes 'Integrations typically take 4-6 weeks to be published'; not a docs statement, not relied on here.)
Partner Network application criteria and approval turnaround.
Any partner program or Marketplace revenue-share fees (docs mention customer-side 'additional fees' only).
Whether an unpublished client has any numeric install/user cap beyond the partner-org-only authorization restriction (none stated).

Whether OAuth clients not tied to a listing (e.g. for Datadog Apps / internal org tools) can be self-created by ordinary org admins (referenced in the scopes doc, but no self-serve creation flow documented in the pages read).

alternatives: API key + application key per organization (the default auth model for everyone else; scoped application keys 'can be assigned any Datadog permission', while OAuth clients get only the limited published scope set)
flavor.recommended: An API-based integration with OAuth ('API with OAuth' configuration method), with the OAuth client attached to an integration listing in the Developer Platform
flavor.why: OAuth exists only inside the partner program: 'OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.' API-based integrations are 'best suited for SaaS-based vendors that can host a service to interact with the Datadog API', and OAuth is mandatory for them: 'Your integration must implement OAuth for authorization' (exceptions only via the Datadog Ecosystems team). Prerequisites: your product must be generally available and must submit telemetry to Datadog.

humanMust: Apply to and be approved by the Datadog Partner Network (Technology Partner track); obtain a partner developer organization
Create the listing in the Developer Platform and configure the OAuth client
Generate the OAuth client secret and record it at generation (it 'is not displayed again'); production credentials are issued at submission and also shown once
Submit the listing for review with production URLs
name: Datadog
nuances: Token lifetimes invert the usual pattern: access tokens have a TTL of 1 hour, but refresh tokens for Marketplace OAuth clients are long-lived with no expiration (TTL of infinity), ending only on user/partner revocation, after which 'the user must reauthorize the integration to generate new refresh and access tokens'.

Secret handling is fragile: test secret differs from production secret (issued at submission), 'only one secret can be active at a time', and rotation is manual, by email: 'If your secret was leaked and needs to be rotated, contact ecosystems@datadog.com.'

Region handling is on you: API endpoints differ per site (api.datadoghq.eu vs .com and others); build URLs from the domain parameter supplied in the handshake and never include the customer's subdomain (site is handshake-only).
Listing content is real work: overview, setup/uninstall instructions, data definitions, support details, and at least one dashboard ('Dashboards are required for all integrations').

Scope ceiling: OAuth clients can only receive the published authorization-scope set, with explicit least-privilege guidance; scoped application keys are the more powerful credential, which is backwards from most providers.
prerequisites: Approved Datadog Technology Partner status and a partner developer organization/sandbox
A generally available product that submits telemetry to Datadog
Listing assets and content (vendor details, SVG wordmark logo, unique integration ID, at least one dashboard)

steps.detail: Join the Datadog Partner Network (Technology Partner track) and get access to a partner developer organization. 'Creating a developer sandbox may take up to one or two business days' (stated).
steps.time: Sandbox up to 1-2 business days (stated); partner approval duration not stated
steps.title: Become an approved Technology Partner

steps.detail: In Integrations > Developer Platform > Publishing > New Listing: offering type, name, vendor details, SVG wordmark logo, unique integration ID.
steps.title: Create the listing

steps.detail: Authorization code flow; PKCE supported. Choose the minimum scopes from Datadog's published scope list (e.g. apm_read, synthetics_read).
steps.title: Implement OAuth 2.0 in your product

steps.detail: Configuration Method tab > 'API with OAuth': OAuth Client Name (should match the integration name), Onboarding URL, one or more Redirect URIs, click 'Generate OAuth Client Secret' for testing credentials (shown once, record it), select minimum scopes, Save.
steps.title: Add OAuth details to the listing

steps.detail: 'Test Authorization' simulates a user clicking 'Connect Accounts' on the integration tile, redirecting to your Onboarding URL with domain and site parameters; complete the flow against your partner developer organization (the only place an unpublished client can be authorized). At runtime the flow must be initiated from Datadog; exchange the code at api.<domain>/oauth2/v1/token for access (1-hour TTL) and refresh tokens (no expiration). If you submit data, request api_keys_write during the handshake and POST /api/v2/api_keys/marketplace to mint the per-org API key.
steps.title: Test with Test Authorization

steps.detail: Replace test URLs with production URLs and submit in the Developer Platform. 'Upon submission in the Developer Platform, production client credentials are provided' (secret shown once). After approval, Datadog publishes the integration as a tile.
steps.time: Submission ~30 min; review duration not stated
steps.title: Submit the listing for review

tagline: The hardest OAuth in the library to even start: Datadog reserves OAuth for approved Technology Partners building official published integrations, so there is no self-serve client at all. Partner approval, a listing review, a flow that must start inside Datadog, and secret rotation by email all stand in front of your first real user.

time.active: ~1-2 days of listing content and flow work once you are a partner
time.total: Unknown: partner approval and listing review durations are not stated in the docs; sandbox alone may take up to 1-2 business days (stated)
